update_triggers: a log producer, event, format, destination, access rule, or retention rule changes
a technology-stack layer or managed provider changes
a security finding or incident changes monitoring needs
the cryptographic or data-classification inventory changes

included: application operational, security, and protected audit records
web, relay, database, container, host, and maintenance layers
Tailscale provider, browser-client, security-test, and CI logging boundaries
excluded: actual log records, private hostnames, addresses, account identifiers, and credentials
unselected future integrations such as bank synchronization and SIEM transport

events: one completion record per routed request except successful health checks
one sanitized record for each unhandled request exception
application and management-command messages that reach the root logger
layers.format: Single-line UTF-8 JSON with timestamp, level, logger, stream, environment, release, request/actor/household correlation IDs, redacted message, allowlisted fields, and exception type plus code locations without exception text.
layers.destination: Process stdout or stderr, captured by Gunicorn and the Compose Docker local logging driver on the Linux VM.
use: correlation with protected audit and security records
layers.access_control: Linux deployment administrators with root-equivalent Docker access; not exposed through the application UI.
layers.retention: Per-container capacity rotation: 20 MiB per file and 5 files, approximately 100 MiB maximum; elapsed retention depends on event volume.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Free-form text is redacted; only allowlisted structured fields are emitted. Raw paths, query strings, request bodies, headers, financial values, emails, cookies, and exception messages are excluded.
layers.integrity_and_availability: JSON encoding prevents record injection, but the local Docker store is administrator-mutable and unavailable after host loss unless preserved during incident response.
layers.limitations: No central metrics or logically separate copy exists; healthy readiness/liveness polling is deliberately omitted.

events: authentication, MFA, recovery, reauthentication, logout, and session-revocation outcomes
rejected CSV lifecycle operations and integrity-blocked exports
layers.format: The same redacting single-line JSON format as operational logs, with stream fixed to security and event set to a stable catalog identifier.
layers.destination: Dedicated Python security handler, then the same process stream and local Docker logging store as operational records.
use: detect repeated authentication failures and sensitive export activity
layers.access_control: Linux deployment administrators with root-equivalent Docker access; records are not available to household members in the UI.
layers.retention: Per-container capacity rotation: 20 MiB per file and 5 files, approximately 100 MiB maximum; elapsed retention depends on event volume.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Submitted identities, passwords, TOTP and recovery codes, session keys, import contents, search text, financial values, and exception messages are excluded or redacted.
layers.integrity_and_availability: Records are JSON-encoded and independently tagged but remain mutable by a host/Docker administrator and share the operational destination.
layers.limitations: This stream is not yet transmitted to a logically separate protected destination; ASVS v5.0.0-16.4.3 remains not started.

layers.stack_layer: Protected financial and security audit stream
events: material household financial, schedule, debt, goal, reserve, import, export, notification, and identity changes
authentication and recovery outcomes needed for household security history
audit detail access and export activity
maintenance actions that change protected credentials or staged data
layers.format: Canonical structured PostgreSQL rows with sequence, UUID, household/actor IDs, timestamp/time zone, action, entity reference, bounded before/after JSON, reason, request ID, previous hash, and SHA-256 event hash.
layers.destination: Separately owned budget_audit PostgreSQL schema, with signed chain-head checkpoints copied to an existing off-VM filesystem.
layers.access_control: Active household membership for summary UI; recent password-plus-MFA verification for detail/export; runtime role can execute only the protected append function; dedicated audit reader is read-only; no application delete/update permission.
layers.retention: Live audit rows and checkpoints are retained for the application lifetime with no delete path. Encrypted backup copies follow 7 daily, 4 weekly, and 12 monthly snapshot retention unless a preserved incident copy supersedes normal pruning.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Protected audit may contain the minimum authorized financial before/after facts and bounded reason, but rejects password, token, cookie, session, recovery-code, and TOTP keys and never stores exports or raw CSV files.
layers.integrity_and_availability: Transactional append, PostgreSQL ownership/trigger controls, per-household SHA-256 chains, daily verification, off-VM HMAC-SHA256 checkpoints, and encrypted backups provide layered detection and recovery.
layers.limitations: Database superusers and host administrators remain trusted; confidentiality relies on host volume controls and encrypted off-VM backups.

events: backup repository initialization, start, completion, validation, retention, and failure outcomes
restore target refusal, start, completion, schema verification, and failure outcomes
Restic and PostgreSQL administrator credential-rotation start, verification, retirement, completion, and failure outcomes
layers.format: Single-line JSON with UTC timestamp, level, stable event identifier, and fixed operator-safe message.
layers.destination: Container stdout/stderr in the Docker local log store; scheduled systemd service wrappers also record command lifecycle in the host journal.
layers.access_control: Linux deployment administrators; maintenance containers are networkless or restricted and receive only task-specific secrets.
layers.retention: Container records use 20 MiB by 5-file rotation. Host service records follow the required 30-day journald policy recorded during deployment review; incident evidence is preserved before normal rollover.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Messages are fixed and omit database rows, repository paths outside generic mount names, credentials, hostnames, private addresses, and command output containing values.
layers.integrity_and_availability: Structured output is locally mutable; protected audit events and signed checkpoints independently cover state-changing rotations and restore comparisons where applicable.
layers.limitations: No remote log destination exists, and the repository cannot prove the live host journald policy before release-candidate deployment.

layers.format: Gunicorn text for process lifecycle plus already formatted Django JSON records for captured application output.
layers.destination: Container stderr/stdout and the Docker local log store.
layers.access_control: Linux deployment administrators with Docker access.
layers.retention: Per-container capacity rotation: 20 MiB per file and 5 files, approximately 100 MiB maximum.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Access logging is disabled to avoid raw URLs, queries, addresses, and user-agent data; captured application output remains subject to the JSON allowlist/redaction policy.
layers.integrity_and_availability: Local Docker storage only; container replacement does not delete rotated driver logs immediately, but host loss does.
layers.limitations: No independent Gunicorn metrics or remote process-log transport is configured.

layers.format: nginx warning/error text to stderr; request access records are disabled.
layers.destination: Container stderr and the Docker local log store.
use: relay availability and upstream failure diagnosis
layers.access_control: Linux deployment administrators with Docker access; the container has no application or infrastructure secrets.
layers.retention: Per-container capacity rotation: 20 MiB per file and 5 files, approximately 100 MiB maximum.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Access logging and forwarded client addresses are disabled; error review must not be copied raw into Git or tickets.
layers.integrity_and_availability: Local Docker storage only and administrator-mutable.
layers.limitations: Tailscale Serve owns browser-facing HTTPS and its request boundary; the relay does not receive the browser address.

events: server lifecycle, recovery, checkpoint, and warning/error records emitted by the pinned image defaults
authentication and database errors at the server boundary
no all-statement or financial-value query logging
layers.format: PostgreSQL server text on stderr using the pinned image's standard configuration.
layers.destination: Database container stderr and the Docker local log store.
layers.access_control: Linux deployment administrators with Docker access; application roles cannot read container logs.
layers.retention: Per-container capacity rotation: 20 MiB per file and 5 files, approximately 100 MiB maximum.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Statement-wide logging is not enabled. Operators must treat database errors as sensitive and must not retain SQL parameters, rows, credentials, or financial values in tickets or Git.
layers.integrity_and_availability: Local Docker storage is separate from PostgreSQL tables but remains on the same VM and administrator-mutable.
layers.limitations: No centralized PostgreSQL log analysis, certificate-authentication log source, or separate security destination exists.

events: stdout and stderr from every one of the 13 production Compose services
layers.format: Docker local driver internal framing and compression around producer-formatted JSON or text records.
layers.destination: Docker-managed local files on the Linux VM; never an application bind mount.
use: bounded local operational review through Docker tooling
source for incident preservation before container or host changes
layers.access_control: Root or explicitly authorized Docker administrators only; Docker group membership is treated as root-equivalent.
layers.retention: Exactly 5 rotated files at 20 MiB each per service under the Compose policy, approximately 100 MiB maximum per service; oldest records are removed on capacity rollover.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: The driver does not redact; every producer must apply its own data-minimization policy before writing stdout/stderr.
layers.integrity_and_availability: Compressed local storage limits disk exhaustion but offers no append-only or off-host integrity guarantee.
layers.limitations: Operational and security streams share this destination, which is a documented ASVS v5.0.0-16.4.3 gap.

layers.stack_layer: Linux VM journal and host security services
events: backup, integrity, notification, and import-cleanup timer/service lifecycle
UFW/firewall and Tailscale daemon events available from the hardened host
layers.format: systemd journal records with trusted host/service metadata and producer text or JSON payload.
layers.destination: Persistent systemd journal on the Linux VM.
use: SSH, firewall, Tailscale, and service incident investigation
layers.access_control: Root and the minimum host journal-reader group; household application accounts receive no host login or journal access.
layers.retention: Required deployment policy is 30 days with a documented size ceiling; the effective journald configuration and available history are recorded during each release review.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Do not enable shell tracing or credential-bearing command lines. Preserve only sanitized summaries outside the host and treat raw journal exports as restricted incident material.
layers.integrity_and_availability: Journal metadata supports ordered local review, but root can modify the host and host loss removes the local copy.
layers.limitations: The repository supplies service units but does not own the host-wide journald configuration; release-candidate evidence must verify it.

layers.scope: approved devices, Linux VM, and Tailscale control plane
events: local Tailscale client/daemon operation and peer contact attempts
provider configuration changes to the tailnet
network flow metadata only if the optional plan feature is deliberately enabled
no application contents or decrypted traffic
layers.format: Provider-defined local client records and Tailscale configuration-audit JSON; optional network flow records contain node and time/flow metadata.
layers.destination: Local approved-device/VM Tailscale logs and Tailscale's central logging service; configuration audit is available in the admin console/API.
layers.access_control: Tailnet users with administration-console access can view configuration logs; scoped API credentials require logs:configuration:read. Local daemon logs require device/host administration.
layers.retention: Tailscale configuration audit logs are retained 90 days. Optional network flow logs, if later enabled, are retained 30 days. Local VM daemon logs follow the 30-day host policy.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Configuration and node metadata are sensitive. Network flow logging does not include traffic content; raw exports remain outside Git and household application records.
layers.integrity_and_availability: Provider configuration logs are off-VM; local client delivery and integrity are not guaranteed, and flow logging is not enabled by this repository.
layers.limitations: Tailscale logs do not replace application security logs and do not satisfy separate transport for the Django security stream.

layers.stack_layer: GitHub Actions CI and security checks
events: test, lint, type, evidence, dependency, browser, backup/restore, upgrade/rollback, and image-scan outcomes
no production runtime logs or secrets
layers.format: GitHub Actions structured run metadata plus step console text and annotations.
layers.destination: GitHub Actions service associated with the repository and immutable commit/run identifiers.
use: failure diagnosis and reviewed dependency/security changes
layers.access_control: Repository access and GitHub authorization; workflows have read-only repository permissions unless a reviewed job explicitly requires more.
layers.retention: 90 days under the repository's current Actions artifact-and-log retention setting; release decisions retain sanitized durable evidence in Git rather than relying on expiring run logs.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Synthetic data only. Raw security reports, real host details, production credentials, and real household data are prohibited; secret scanning and GitHub masking are defense in depth.
layers.integrity_and_availability: Provider-managed run records bind to commit SHAs, but expiring or provider-controlled logs are not the durable release record.
layers.limitations: CI results do not verify the private Linux VM or real devices and must not be relabeled as release-candidate evidence.

events: browser-local developer console and network diagnostics only when an operator deliberately opens them
no application-managed client telemetry, analytics, or persistent browser log upload
layers.destination: Volatile browser process/profile on the approved device; no application or third-party analytics destination.
use: short-lived troubleshooting on an approved device
layers.access_control: The signed-in device user and device administrator.
layers.retention: Not centrally retained; normally ends with the diagnostic session or browser-managed local history. Any capture is restricted and deleted after sanitized findings are recorded.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Do not preserve cookies, storage, URLs containing sensitive queries, financial payloads, screenshots of real data, or private network details.
layers.integrity_and_availability: No server-side completeness or integrity guarantee exists because client telemetry is intentionally absent.
layers.limitations: Browser diagnostics are not monitoring and cannot substitute for application/server records.

layers.stack_layer: Disposable security and compatibility test output
layers.scope: local development and CI synthetic targets
events: ZAP, Playwright, authorization, session, CSV, financial-logic, audit-integrity, network, restore, rotation, and upgrade/rollback diagnostics
layers.format: Tool-native raw reports in ignored ephemeral locations; machine-validated sanitized JSON/Markdown summaries for retained evidence.
layers.destination: Ignored security-reports directories, disposable containers/volumes, and CI run logs; sanitized findings and evidence schemas are committed only after review.
layers.access_control: Developer or release owner for raw output; repository readers receive sanitized committed artifacts only.
layers.retention: Raw output lasts only through triage/retest and is deleted with the disposable target; CI copies expire after 90 days. Sanitized committed findings and supersession records remain in Git history.
layers.sensitive_data_policy: Synthetic data only. Raw reports may still expose attack payloads, cookies, fixture details, or private topology and therefore never enter source control.
layers.integrity_and_availability: Sanitized evidence binds to candidate commit and preserves supersession; raw ephemeral output has no durable guarantee.
layers.limitations: A structurally ready matrix or development run is not a release pass.

Literal structured security event fields in application Python outside migrations and tests
Literal dotted action keyword values in production Python outside migrations and tests
Literal structured log and failure event arguments in the production backup, restore, Restic rotation, and PostgreSQL administrator rotation shell scripts

known_gaps.current_state: Django security records are tagged but stored with operational logs in the same host-local Docker logging system.
known_gaps.required_action: Transmit security logs to a logically separate protected analysis and escalation destination without forwarding prohibited data.

known_gaps.current_state: The repository defines required 30-day host-journal retention, but the live VM setting and available history cannot be proven before deployment.
known_gaps.required_action: Record sanitized journald retention, capacity, access-group, and sample timer/SSH/firewall/Tailscale event checks for the selected release candidate.

known_gaps.current_state: No SIEM, remote alert pipeline, or independent operational-log archive receives Django, PostgreSQL, Docker, or host security records.
known_gaps.required_action: Select a household-appropriate protected destination, minimize fields, restrict readers, test delivery/failure alerting, and define incident escalation before marking separate logging verified.

known_gaps.current_state: Tailscale configuration audit logging is provider-enabled, but optional network flow logging is not enabled or assumed by this repository.
known_gaps.required_action: If the selected plan and household privacy decision enable flow logging, record that change, the 30-day provider retention, reader roles, export destination, and data-minimization review before use.
